headline: Democrat Scott Colom wins Mississippi Senate seat
standfirst: A historic upset ends decades of Republican control in the state's Senate race.

steps.label: What happened
steps.text: Democrat Scott Colom defeated Republican incumbent Cindy Hyde-Smith by a very narrow margin.

steps.label: How we got here
steps.text: The result followed over a week of vote counting in a state that last elected a Democrat in 1982.

steps.label: Why it matters
steps.text: Colom is the first Black senator elected in Mississippi since the Reconstruction era.

steps.label: What to watch
steps.text: Observers will watch for how this shift impacts the balance of power in the Senate.

caption:
Scott Colom has defeated incumbent Cindy Hyde-Smith in a historic Mississippi Senate election result.

This victory marks the first time Mississippi has sent a Democrat to the Senate in over forty years. It also represents a major milestone as Colom becomes the state's first Black senator elected since the Reconstruction period. The outcome was only confirmed after a week of intense vote counting.
